userStories.title: Webhook configuration writes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record committed outbound webhook configuration creates, updates and deletes atomically with their AuditEntry.

**Motivation** — A webhook a project admin pointed at a new URL, a skill source a global admin deleted, a skill enabled on a project, a dead outbox event an admin replayed, a nightly purge that deleted read notifications, and a seeder that rolled back an admin's edit of a system role still leave no entry.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

- **Each service records at its own write, through `audited`.** None of the changed services writes `AuditEntry` today. `WebhookService`, `SkillsService`, `NotificationPreferencesService`, `TicketWatchService` and `OutboxAdminService` take `AuditRecorder` as their last constructor parameter. Each write becomes `this.audit.audited(() => <the existing write>, (result) => entries)`. Where the service already runs `this.txManager.run(() => write)`, that call becomes `this.audit.audited(() => write, entriesOf)`, which opens the same transaction. Where the result says nothing was written (a `null` or `false` repository answer, a count of 0), `entriesOf` returns `[]` and the service raises its existing error after `audited` resolves.
- **A webhook entry never prints the URL or the secret.** A URL may carry a token in its path or query, and the secret is the HMAC key. Create records `created`, update records `fieldsSummary(dto)` (field names only), delete records `deleted`.
- **The global webhook delete records the webhook's project.** `DELETE /webhooks/:id` has no slug. `WebhookService.remove` already reads the webhook before deleting, so its entry carries `projectId` from that row.
- **A webhook update with no field records `summary` `null`.** `fieldsSummary` answers `undefined` for an empty patch, so the entry is written with no summary, as `label.update` does.

Entry contract: create uses key webhook.create, resourceType webhook, resourceId returned webhook id, projectId the project, summary created. update uses webhook.update on that webhook/project, summary fieldsSummary(dto). removeForProject and remove use webhook.delete on that webhook with its projectId, summary deleted. Actor, origin and approval come from current context, not new service parameters. Run repository writes through audited so a rejected record rolls back create/update/delete; keep URL checking before the write and retain existing 400/404 behavior, generated secret, return values and projections. Refused writes emit nothing.

**Scope** — In: webhook.service.ts; webhook.service.spec.ts (both direct constructors pass mockAuditRecorder); webhook-routes.spec.ts (AuditRecorder provider); new test/integration/audit/audit-webhooks.integration.spec.ts. Preserve all existing assertions. Out: skills (US-002), preference/watch/retry (US-003), retention/health (US-004), seeder (US-005); webhook sends, URL/secret summaries, contract changes and global-delete audit-failure test are excluded. Do not add the coverage guard or walker.

**Interface** — `WebhookService` constructor — Baseline: `(webhookRepo, urlGuard)`. Target: `(webhookRepo, urlGuard, audit: AuditRecorder)`. `create`, `update`, `remove` and `removeForProject` record the contract's entries; their checks, errors and return values are unchanged.

Read-only: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }` — `src/audit/audit-recorder.service.ts`. `record` throws for a key outside the catalog and outside a transaction (`txManager.isInTransaction()`), and reads the actor, origin, approval and correlation id from `currentContext()`. `audited` runs `fn` inside `txManager.run`, which an inner `txManager.run` joins. `fieldsSummary(patch)` — `src/audit/audit-summary.ts`: sorted names of the defined fields, `fields: a, b`, or `undefined` for none.

Testing: boot real AppModule with bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }), root first/Owner, dev created through admin/users and developer membership, wh-audit/WHA plus wh-other/WHO. Each case owns its webhook fixture. Use IP-literal URLs from the ACs; do not depend on DNS. resetThrottle in beforeEach, query fixtureDb(app).auditEntry by resourceId and key, compare before/after counts for unchanged. Audit-failure spies reject only the first webhook writer-key call with Error('audit down'), delegate all others to the original and restore afterward. Use the real recorder in integration, not mockAuditRecorder. Unit/DI compatibility uses the shared stub. Run scoped Vitest integration outside the sandbox with a real test Postgres and preserve shared DB gating.

userStories.title: Skill writes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record source create/update/delete and project skill enable/disable in the same transaction as their catalog writes.

**Motivation** — A webhook a project admin pointed at a new URL, a skill source a global admin deleted, a skill enabled on a project, a dead outbox event an admin replayed, a nightly purge that deleted read notifications, and a seeder that rolled back an admin's edit of a system role still leave no entry.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

- **Each service records at its own write, through `audited`.** None of the changed services writes `AuditEntry` today. `WebhookService`, `SkillsService`, `NotificationPreferencesService`, `TicketWatchService` and `OutboxAdminService` take `AuditRecorder` as their last constructor parameter. Each write becomes `this.audit.audited(() => <the existing write>, (result) => entries)`. Where the service already runs `this.txManager.run(() => write)`, that call becomes `this.audit.audited(() => write, entriesOf)`, which opens the same transaction. Where the result says nothing was written (a `null` or `false` repository answer, a count of 0), `entriesOf` returns `[]` and the service raises its existing error after `audited` resolves.
- **A skill source entry names its status and skill count.** Create and update record `<verb>, status <status>, skills <n>` (verb `created` or `updated`; `n` is the number of skills on the returned source). Git coordinates are not secret, but they are already the source row; the summary does not repeat them. Both the resolved and the `RESOLVE_FAILED` outcome of create, and both outcomes of update, are writes and record.
- **Enable and disable record every successful call.** `enableProjectSkill` upserts the row (it rewrites `enabledById`), and `disableProjectSkill` answers `true` for a skill that exists whether or not a row was removed. Changing the repository's answer to tell the two apart is out of scope; a repeated disable records a second `skill.project.disable`.

Entry contract: createSource -> skill.source.create, resourceType skill-source, source id, projectId null, created, status <status>, skills <n>. Both updateSource write branches -> skill.source.update on skill-source/source id/global with updated, status <status>, skills <n>. deleteSource -> skill.source.delete on skill-source/source id/global with deleted. enableProjectSkill -> skill.project.enable on skill/skill id/project id with enabled; disableProjectSkill -> skill.project.disable on skill/skill id/project id with disabled. Read status and skill count from the repository's result. Null/false result callbacks return [] and the existing not-found exceptions are raised after audited resolves. Keep resolver IO, GitHub URL parsing and ownership checks outside write transactions. Preserve duplicate/name conflicts, unique-violation handling, return values and all existing errors. A rejected record rolls back the catalog write, including nested skill replacement, deletion and project enable.

**Scope** — In: skills.service.ts; skills.service.spec.ts constructor/stub cleanup and callback-aware AC13; new test/integration/audit/audit-skills.integration.spec.ts. Out: webhooks (US-001), preferences/watch/outbox retry (US-003), retention/health (US-004), seeder (US-005). Do not change the repository's repeated-disable semantics. Tests for updateSource's unique-violation race, missing-source update, missing-skill disable and name-conflicting create are excluded; keep those pre-record error paths unchanged.

**Interface** — `SkillsService` constructor — Baseline: `(catalog, resolver, txManager)`. Target: `(catalog, resolver, audit: AuditRecorder)`; `txManager` is dropped, because every `this.txManager.run(…)` it served becomes `this.audit.audited(…)` (which opens the same transaction) and a private member left unread fails the type check. The three `this.txManager.run(…)` writes of `createSource` and `updateSource`, and the one of `deleteSource`, become `this.audit.audited(…)`; `enableProjectSkill` and `disableProjectSkill` wrap their repository call in `audited`.

Read-only: `SkillCatalogRepository.createSource`, `markResolveFailed`, `replaceSourceSkills` (each answers the source or `null`), `deleteSource` (`boolean`), `enableProjectSkill` (the skill or `null`), `disableProjectSkill` (`boolean`) — `src/skills/prisma-skill-catalog.repository.ts`; unchanged. `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }` — `src/audit/audit-recorder.service.ts`.

Testing: boot real AppModule using bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }); root registers first as Owner, dev is created through admin/users and is developer on sk-audit/SKA. Before each case resetThrottle and delete projectSkill, skill, skillSource rows. Spy on the booted SKILL_RESOLVER resolve; never contact GitHub. Source body is { gitUrl: 'https://github.com/acme/skills', ref: 'main', path: <per-AC path> }; default fixture path skills/a resolves { sha: 's1', skills: [{ name: 'audit-a', description: 'd', dir: 'skills/a' }] }. Each case creates its own source, even when referring to AC1's input, and enables its own skill first when required. Query stored entries through fixtureDb(app) by resourceId and key. Record-failure spies reject the first matching writer-key call with Error('audit down'), delegate other calls and restore afterward. For AC13 use a local recorder that executes fn then entriesOf and records returned entries; mockAuditRecorder's default audited intentionally does not evaluate entriesOf. Keep all prior unit assertions while replacing new SkillsService(catalog, resolver, txManager) with new SkillsService(catalog, resolver, mockAuditRecorder) and removing the unused transaction stub/import. Run integration with the shared DB gate outside the sandbox.

userStories.title: Preferences, ticket watch and outbox retry are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit supplied notification-preference switches, explicit ticket watch settings and administrative outbox retries without auditing inbox read marks; category, watch and retry writes are atomic with their entries, while master-switch atomicity remains package-dependent.

**Motivation** — A webhook a project admin pointed at a new URL, a skill source a global admin deleted, a skill enabled on a project, a dead outbox event an admin replayed, a nightly purge that deleted read notifications, and a seeder that rolled back an admin's edit of a system role still leave no entry.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

- **Each service records at its own write, through `audited`.** None of the changed services writes `AuditEntry` today. `WebhookService`, `SkillsService`, `NotificationPreferencesService`, `TicketWatchService` and `OutboxAdminService` take `AuditRecorder` as their last constructor parameter. Each write becomes `this.audit.audited(() => <the existing write>, (result) => entries)`. Where the service already runs `this.txManager.run(() => write)`, that call becomes `this.audit.audited(() => write, entriesOf)`, which opens the same transaction. Where the result says nothing was written (a `null` or `false` repository answer, a count of 0), `entriesOf` returns `[]` and the service raises its existing error after `audited` resolves.
- **A preferences update records one entry naming the changed switches.** The summary is `fields: <names>`, the distinct names sorted in code-unit order (so the uppercase categories come before `emailEnabled`: `fields: ASSIGNED.inApp, MENTIONED.email, emailEnabled`), where a name is `emailEnabled` or `<CATEGORY>.<channel>` (`MENTIONED.email`, `ASSIGNED.inApp`). Values are never printed. A body that supplies no switch records nothing. `NotificationPreferencesService.update` runs its whole body inside `audited`: the master switch goes through `IPreferenceService.updatePreference` (`@nathapp/nestjs-notify`), whose store joins the ambient transaction only if it writes through the proxied `PrismaService`. So the category rows and the entry are atomic, and the master switch is atomic with them only when the package store joins.
- **Watch and unwatch record on the ticket.** `ticket.watch.set` with summary `watching`, and `ticket.watch.unset` with summary `muted` (an unwatch sets `muted`; the row stays).
- **An outbox retry records on the event.** Summary `retried <type>, was <status>`, `projectId` from the event (`event.projectId ?? null`: `OutboxEventDomain.projectId` is typed `string` but is `null` at runtime for a global type). A reset that changed no row (`resetForRetry` answered 0, a concurrent change) records nothing and answers the existing 409.
- **Read marks are bookkeeping.** `POST /me/notifications/:id/read` and `POST /me/notifications/read-all` change only the caller's own inbox state. They record nothing. Preferences and ticket watch are recorded: each is a setting that changes what the system later delivers to the caller.

Entry contract: notification.preference.update on resourceType user, resourceId caller's user id, projectId null, names-only summary; ticket.watch.set/unset on resourceType ticket, resourceId resolved ticket id, projectId project; outbox.retry on resourceType outbox-event, resourceId event id, projectId pre-read event.projectId ?? null. The :eventId route parameter denotes the OutboxEvent row's id passed to findById/resetForRetry, not the eventId deduplication metadata field. Record under the current route principal/rest context; do not pass actors through new service arguments. Keep update's write ordering, inner category transaction/txnClient use, watch ref resolution and returned state, retry eligibility, both 409 messages and 404 unchanged. A rejected record rolls back category rows, watcher mutation or reset; do not promise master-switch rollback when its package store does not join. Empty preferences must leave storage and audit unchanged.

**Scope** — In: notification-preferences.service.ts, ticket-watch.service.ts, outbox-admin.service.ts and their unit specs; append mockAuditRecorder to each direct constructor, preserving existing assertions; add the callback-executing zero-reset unit case in outbox-admin.service.spec.ts; append mockAuditRecorder to the direct OutboxAdminService construction in test/integration/outbox/outbox-relay.integration.spec.ts; create test/integration/audit/audit-preferences-watch-outbox.integration.spec.ts. Out: webhook configuration (US-001), skills (US-002), retention/health plus relay-spec global module wiring (US-004), seeder (US-005). Read marks, derived watcher ensures, notification fan-out/email, master-switch atomicity repair or its rejection test, duplicate categories, switchless items and the excluded unwatch sibling tests remain out. Coordinate the relay-spec constructor edit with US-004's independent global-provider edit without introducing a dependency.

**Interface** — `NotificationPreferencesService` constructor — Baseline: `(prisma, txManager, packagePrefs, email)`. Target: `(prisma, txManager, packagePrefs, email, audit: AuditRecorder)`. `update`'s body runs inside `audited`.
`TicketWatchService` constructor — Baseline: `(repo)`. Target: `(repo, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
`OutboxAdminService` constructor — Baseline: `(outboxRepo)`. Target: `(outboxRepo, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
Read-only: `TicketWatchersRepository.watch`, `unwatch`, `state`, `findTicketIdByRef` — `src/notifications/ticket-watchers.repository.ts`; unchanged. `PrismaOutboxRepository.findById`, `resetForRetry(id, now): Promise<number>`, `deleteTerminalBefore` — `src/outbox/prisma-outbox.repository.ts`; unchanged. `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`.

Testing: boot real AppModule with bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }); root first/Owner, dev via POST /api/admin/users then developer on nt-audit/NTA. Root creates NTA-1 and NTA-2 without assignee or dev mentions so dev has no watcher row initially. ResetThrottle in beforeEach. Store outbox fixtures through fixtureDb(app) with type ticket_event, unique eventId evt-<n>, projectId and status; read actual audit rows by resourceId/key. Notification fixture for read-all uses dev userId, category ASSIGNED, kind ticket_assigned, title t, link /, sourceType ticket_event, sourceId s-<n> and unread readAt. Compare counts before/after unchanged cases. Audit rejection spies reject only the first matching key with Error('audit down'), delegate all others and restore. AC15 requires a local recorder executing fn then entriesOf and recording returned entries, not the shared fn-only stub. Preserve shared DB gating and run the scoped PG suite outside the sandbox.

userStories.title: Retention purges and fleet health episodes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit nonempty retention deletions and health episode openings/closures with their system actors and transaction boundaries.

**Motivation** — A webhook a project admin pointed at a new URL, a skill source a global admin deleted, a skill enabled on a project, a dead outbox event an admin replayed, a nightly purge that deleted read notifications, and a seeder that rolled back an admin's edit of a system role still leave no entry.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

- **A retention purge records one entry per step per run that deleted rows.** This is the `EnrollmentRetentionProcessor` precedent from audit-fleet-system: `audited(() => delete, (count) => count === 0 ? [] : [{ …, resourceId: 'all', projectId: null }])`. The outbox purge records `purged <n> terminal events` on `outbox-event`. The notification purge records `purged <n> read notifications` on `notification` and `purged <n> closed health alerts` on `fleet-health-alert`, both under `system.notification.retention`. Each step already logs and swallows its own failure, so a rejected `record` rolls that step's delete back, is logged, and the next step runs.
- **The health detector records each opened episode in its existing transaction, and closes per run.** An opened episode records `system.health.detect` on `fleet-health-alert` with the alert id and summary `opened <kind>`, inside the `txManager.run` that already writes the episode and its outbox event. A close of one or more episodes records one entry with `resourceId` `all` and summary `closed <n>`, through `audited` around `repo.close`; a close that closed nothing records nothing.

Entry contract: outbox purge uses system.outbox.retention/outbox-event/all/null/purged <n> terminal events; notification steps use system.notification.retention/notification/all/null/purged <n> read notifications and system.notification.retention/fleet-health-alert/all/null/purged <n> closed health alerts. Health open/close use system.health.detect/fleet-health-alert with alert id or all respectively, projectId null. Actor/origin are SYSTEM/outbox/system, SYSTEM/notification/system, SYSTEM/health/system from the existing runAsSystemWriter entry wrappers, not custom context construction. On each open call record after outbox.record within the existing txManager.run only when repo.open returned an alert id. If recording rejects, alert and outbox roll back and detect rejects for retry on the next tick. Do not collapse purge steps or all opens into one new transaction. Keep count returns, plan calculation, boot grace, schedules, logging and failure handling unchanged. Configurable days unset/nonpositive still skip that delete; closed health alerts keep their fixed 30-day step. This existing disabled-retention behavior is preserved by review; the spec excludes adding an unset-days test and new integration fixtures set both days before boot.

**Scope** — In: outbox-retention.processor.ts, notification-retention.processor.ts, fleet/fleet-health.detector.ts, their existing unit specs, outbox.module.spec.ts, outbox-relay.integration.spec.ts and producer-atomicity.integration.spec.ts DI compatibility, plus new test/integration/audit/audit-delivery-system.integration.spec.ts. Out: webhooks (US-001), skills (US-002), preference/watch/retry mutations and relay-spec direct admin constructor (US-003), role seeding (US-005); delivery bookkeeping, coverage guard/walker, changed windows and the excluded unset-days, separate closed-alert purge rejection and episode-close rejection tests.

**Interface** — `OutboxRetentionProcessor` constructor — Baseline: `(repository, config)`. Target: `(repository, config, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
`NotificationRetentionProcessor` constructor — Baseline: `(repo, config, healthAlerts)`. Target: `(repo, config, healthAlerts, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
`FleetHealthDetector` constructor — Baseline: `(repo, outbox, txManager, cfg)`. Target: `(repo, outbox, txManager, cfg, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
Read-only: `NotificationsRepository.purgeRead(before): Promise<number>` and `FleetHealthAlertsRepository.open`, `close(ids, now): Promise<number>`, `purgeClosed(before): Promise<number>` — unchanged. `runAsSystemWriter(writer, fn)`, `runAsSystem(component, fn)` — `src/action-context/action-context.ts`. `OutboxRetentionProcessor.scheduledPurge`, `NotificationRetentionProcessor.scheduledPurge` and `FleetHealthDetector.detect` already run as their component; `SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap` already runs as `seed`. Unchanged. The precedent for a retention entry: `EnrollmentRetentionProcessor` (`src/fleet/runners/enrollment-retention.processor.ts:38`), `audited(() => delete, (count) => count === 0 ? [] : [entry])` with `resourceId` `all`.

Test wiring: both outbox-retention.processor.spec.ts testing modules gain an AuditRecorder/mockAuditRecorder provider. outbox.module.spec.ts's @Global FakePrismaModule must provide AND export AuditRecorder/mockAuditRecorder. Add an equivalent @Global audit-stub module to outbox-relay.integration.spec.ts, and replace producer-atomicity.integration.spec.ts's root-only audit provider with a global fake module visible to imported OutboxModule; preserve existing assertions. Append mockAuditRecorder to notification-retention.processor.spec.ts's constructor and both fleet-health.detector.spec.ts constructors. GlobalStubsModule already covers other feature-module tests. Do not stub the recorder in the NEW audit integration suite.

Testing: boot real AppModule with bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }), root first/Owner and dev created through admin/users. Set OUTBOX_RETENTION_DAYS and NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_DAYS to '30' before boot and restore afterward. Before each case resetThrottle and delete auditEntry, outboxEvent, notification, fleetHealthAlert and runner rows. Create each AC's own old rows 40 days ago; outbox fixtures must explicitly set updatedAt as well as type, eventId evt-<n>, projectId and status. Read-notification fixture uses dev userId, ASSIGNED/ticket_assigned, title t, link /, ticket_event/s-<n> and old readAt; old health alert uses runner_offline/old-<n> and old closedAt. Exercise app.get(...).scheduledPurge() and detect(now) past boot grace, reading stored AuditEntry via fixtureDb(app). Fail only the first record call matching that writer's key with Error('audit down'), delegating subsequent calls; AC6 depends on the second notification step recording successfully. Restore spies after each case. Verify open rollback on BOTH alert and its outbox event. For the failure-table retry criterion, restore the rejected-record spy before invoking detect(now) again against the same still-offline runner fixture; the failed transaction must not leave an episode that suppresses that retry. Assert the existing outbox Logger.error message in the same audit-failure fixture without adding a separate closed-health-alert rejection test. Use shared DB gating and run the integration suite outside the sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given two published outbox events with updatedAt 40 days ago and 30-day retention, when app.get(OutboxRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs, then it leaves one entry for all with key system.outbox.retention, resourceType outbox-event, projectId null, actorType SYSTEM, actorId outbox, origin system and summary purged 2 terminal events.

[integration] Given no terminal outbox event older than 30 days, when app.get(OutboxRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs, then it resolves with the count of system.outbox.retention entries unchanged.

[integration] Given one dead outbox event with updatedAt 40 days ago, when app.get(OutboxRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs while record is spied to reject system.outbox.retention, then it resolves and that event still exists.

[integration] Given one notification of dev's with readAt 40 days ago, when app.get(NotificationRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs, then it leaves one entry with key system.notification.retention, resourceType notification, resourceId all, actorType SYSTEM, actorId notification and summary purged 1 read notifications.

[integration] Given one fleet health alert with closedAt 40 days ago, when app.get(NotificationRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs, then it leaves one entry with key system.notification.retention, resourceType fleet-health-alert, resourceId all and summary purged 1 closed health alerts.

[integration] Given one notification read 40 days ago and one health alert closed 40 days ago, when app.get(NotificationRetentionProcessor).scheduledPurge() runs while record is spied to reject its first system.notification.retention call, then it resolves, the notification still exists and the health alert is gone.

[integration] Given now past boot grace and one enabled runner whose lastSeenAt is older than runnerOfflineSec, when app.get(FleetHealthDetector).detect(now) runs, then it opens one runner_offline episode and leaves one entry for that alert's id with key system.health.detect, resourceType fleet-health-alert, projectId null, actorType SYSTEM, actorId health, origin system and summary opened runner_offline.
[integration] Given an existing episode for a runner still offline, when detect(now) runs a second time, then the count of system.health.detect entries is unchanged.

[integration] Given an offline runner, when detect(now) runs while record is spied to reject system.health.detect, then it rejects with no open FleetHealthAlert for that runner and no fleet_health_alert outbox event for it.

[integration] Given detect(now) opened a runner_offline episode for an offline runner, when the runner's lastSeenAt is set to now and detect(now) runs again, then it closes the episode and leaves one entry for all with key system.health.detect and summary closed 1.
[integration] Given every runner online and no open episode, when detect(now) runs, then the count of system.health.detect entries is unchanged.

Given a nonempty terminal-event purge and AuditRecorder.record rejecting with Error('audit down'), when OutboxRetentionProcessor.scheduledPurge() runs, then Logger.error receives a message equal to Outbox retention purge failed, will retry next run: audit down, preserving the existing error log contract.

Given an enabled offline runner whose episode-open transaction rolled back after record rejected, when the record spy is restored and the next FleetHealthDetector.detect(now) runs past boot grace with that runner still offline, then it opens a runner_offline episode with its fleet_health_alert outbox event and system.health.detect entry.

userStories.title: The system role seeder is audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record each bootstrap role creation or restoration as role.manage attributed to SYSTEM/seed, atomically per role write.

**Motivation** — A webhook a project admin pointed at a new URL, a skill source a global admin deleted, a skill enabled on a project, a dead outbox event an admin replayed, a nightly purge that deleted read notifications, and a seeder that rolled back an admin's edit of a system role still leave no entry.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

- **The seeder records `role.manage` as `SYSTEM/seed`.** `seed` is a keyless system actor id (`action-context.ts:70`), so there is no `system.*` key to record under. `role.manage` is the key `RoleAdminService` records for an admin's role writes, and the actor (`SYSTEM/seed`, origin `system`) tells them apart. A created role records `seeded`; a restored role records `restored from seed, ` followed by `fieldsSummary(patch)` (`fields: name, permissions, scope` for the locked `owner`, `fields: name, scope` for an unlocked role). A role that needs no patch records nothing. Each write runs through `audited`. Adding a `system.role.seed` catalog key is out of scope.

Entry contract: role.manage, resourceType role, resourceId created or restored role id, projectId null; actorType SYSTEM, actorId seed, origin system from the existing onApplicationBootstrap runAsSystem('seed', …). Wrap createRole and update individually in audited, preserving validation of ALL seeds before the first write. Keep current patch rules: locked roles restore permissions/name/scope; unlocked roles preserve permissions but restore name/scope. Keep log lines and no-patch return unchanged. When record rejects, the role write rolls back and onApplicationBootstrap rejects as any seed write failure already does; do not swallow the failure or wrap all roles in one transaction.

**Scope** — In: system-role.seeder.ts; system-role.seeder.spec.ts (all constructor calls append mockAuditRecorder, keep existing assertions and add callback-aware seeded-entry AC4); permissions/test-helpers/permission-fixtures.ts ensureSystemRoles constructor; test/integration/permissions/system-roles.integration.spec.ts constructor; new test/integration/audit/audit-role-seeder.integration.spec.ts. Out: webhook (US-001), skill (US-002), preference/watch/retry (US-003), retention/health (US-004); role catalog additions, changed seed definitions, permission checks, bootstrap restore rules and coverage guard/walker. Fixtures use a mock recorder only to retain fixture behavior; the new audit integration must use the real app-provided seeder and recorder.

**Interface** — `SystemRoleSeeder` constructor — Baseline: `(seeds, roles)`. Target: `(seeds, roles, audit: AuditRecorder)`.
Read-only: `RoleRepository.createRole(input): Promise<RoleDomain>`, `update(id, patch)` — `src/permissions/permissions.types.ts`; unchanged. `fieldsSummary(patch)` — `src/audit/audit-summary.ts`: sorted names of the defined fields, `fields: a, b`, or `undefined` for none. `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`. `SystemRoleSeeder.onApplicationBootstrap` already runs as `seed`. Unchanged.

Testing: boot real AppModule against PG using bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }). Resolve SystemRoleSeeder from app, not new SystemRoleSeeder with stubs, for integration. Before each integration AC clear all auditEntry rows and restore viewer's seeded name so boot-generated entries are not counted; use fixtureDb(app) for setup and stored-entry queries. Restore owner state between cases as needed. resetThrottle in beforeEach when using shared HTTP setup. Audit-failure spy rejects only the first role.manage call with Error('audit down'), delegates other calls and restores afterward. The seeded create unit case uses a valid RoleSeed for audit-role, findOne -> null, createRole -> id r-1, and a local audited implementation that executes fn then records entriesOf(result); the shared stub alone cannot exercise that callback. Existing permission module stubs already provide AuditRecorder globally. Run DB-backed scoped tests outside the sandbox using the shared DB gate.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given audit entries cleared in beforeEach and the viewer role's name set to Renamed viewer through fixtureDb(app), when app.get(SystemRoleSeeder).onApplicationBootstrap() runs, then it leaves one entry for viewer's role id with key role.manage, resourceType role, projectId null, actorType SYSTEM, actorId seed, origin system and summary restored from seed, fields: name, scope.
[integration] Given no role changed after seeding, when app.get(SystemRoleSeeder).onApplicationBootstrap() runs a second time, then the count of role.manage entries with actorId seed is unchanged.

[integration] Given viewer's role name set to Renamed again through fixtureDb(app), when app.get(SystemRoleSeeder).onApplicationBootstrap() runs while record is spied to reject role.manage, then it rejects and viewer's name remains Renamed again.

[unit] Given seed audit-role, a stub repository whose findOne resolves null and createRole resolves a RoleDomain with id r-1, and a stub recorder whose audited executes fn then records entriesOf(result), when new SystemRoleSeeder([seed], repo, recorder).onApplicationBootstrap() runs, then recorder.record is called once with key role.manage, resourceType role, resourceId r-1, projectId null and summary seeded.

[integration] Given owner's role name set to Renamed owner through fixtureDb(app), when app.get(SystemRoleSeeder).onApplicationBootstrap() runs, then it leaves one entry for owner's role id with key role.manage, actorId seed and summary restored from seed, fields: name, permissions, scope.

routing.reasoning: A standard recorder addition to one service with constructor/fixture compatibility, but it mutates system roles and restores locked owner permissions at bootstrap, requiring the security override and strict isolated TDD.

The five binding stories are independent implementation slices in apps/api, delivered together as one capability; none introduces a symbol another needs. The codebase-memory MCP server is unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct reads and targeted text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. No runtime or database tests were executed while drafting this PRD.

AUTHORITATIVE ARCHITECTURE AND RULES
The generated stack hints in the prompt are not authoritative: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:22 identifies NestJS 12 with Fastify via Nathapp, Prisma 7, Vitest and oxlint, not a generic Express implementation. The HTTP test helper can use Express by default or opt into Fastify (apps/api/test/helpers/http-app.ts:14,28). RISKS, COMPATIBILITY AND DELIVERY
The highest risks are writing audit after commit, stubs hiding a skipped entriesOf callback, recording phantom entries for null/false/0 results, changing exceptions by throwing too early/late, accidentally logging secrets through summaries, breaking imported-module DI tests, and tests observing unrelated seed/fixture audit rows. Mitigate with real rollback assertions plus callback-focused unit cases, exact field-name summaries and narrow constructor/provider updates. Audit failure intentionally turns an otherwise successful write into an error with rollback; retention is the deliberate logged/swallowed exception, health detect and seed bootstrap reject. Master-switch atomicity is intentionally qualified by the package store, not repaired here. Outbox event projectId must be normalized with ?? null despite its domain typing. There are no schema, migration, DTO, route-status, @Requires, OpenAPI, generated-client or permission changes, no backfill, and no new abstractions. Deploy the service changes and constructor/test wiring together atop existing audit-core storage; no data migration or feature toggle is required. Existing rows receive no retrospective entries; only committed writes from deployment onward record.
